hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: A string is almost-palindromic if at most one character modification makes it a palindrome.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: Consider expanding outward from every possible center, including single-character and between-character centers.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Count mismatched character pairs as you expand, stopping when mismatches exceed one.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def longestAlmostPalindrome(s: str) -> int:
    n = len(s)
    if n <= 2:
        return n
    max_len = 1
    def expand(left: int, right: int) -> int:
        mismatches = 0
        l, r = left, right
        cur_len = 0
        while l >= 0 and r < n:
            if s[l] != s[r]:
                mismatches += 1
                if mismatches > 1:
                    break
            cur_len = r - l + 1
            l -= 1
            r += 1
        return cur_len

    for i in range(n):
        max_len = max(max_len, expand(i, i))
        max_len = max(max_len, expand(i, i + 1))
    return max_len
```

complexity.notes: Expanding from 2n - 1 center positions takes at most O(n) per center.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: A brute force approach would exceed time limits by redundantly reprocessing states.
